title: 7 best answering services for small business
summary: Seven answering services compared on price, coverage, and what each actually handles. Find AI, human, and hybrid options, with real starting prices.
body_markdown:
[Customer service expectations](https://www.quo.com/blog/customer-service-expectations/) are at an all-time high, so if a caller reaches your voicemail, you’ve probably already lost them. That’s why answering services are essential for growing businesses.


The best answering service for a small business depends on how many of your calls actually need a person. If most are routine questions, scheduling, and lead capture, an AI service starting around $25 to $200 a month will handle them and cost a fraction of the alternative. If most need judgment, a human or hybrid service running $250 to $1,725+ a month is worth the money.


If it feels like there are a million answering services to choose from, you can use this guide to help narrow down your search. I’ve tested and compiled the best phone answering services — plus prices, features, and limitations — so you can find a fit for your team.

##


Quick picks


Short on time? Here’s a quick rundown of your best options:


- **Quo’s Sona:** Best AI service built into a phone system if you already pay for a business phone and don’t want a second vendor.
- **Rosie and Goodcall:** Best affordable options for a standalone AI service.
- **Smith.ai and Abby Connect:** Best options for a hybrid service with AI answering for routine calls and live agents for escalations.
- **Ruby:** Best high-touch option for a live call and chat answering service that acts like a front desk employee.
- **AnswerConnect:** Best live answering service for startups with live chat.


Choose a service with a free tier first if you’re not sure which of the above you want. Smith.ai and Quo both let you test with real calls before paying.


##


7 best answering services for SMBs: In-depth analysis


We’ll start with the strongest option on our list for small and growing businesses:


### 1. Sona: Best for growing businesses


#### Pros


- Works natively within Quo for full visibility
- Direct integrations with HubSpot, Salesforce, Jobber, Zapier, Make, and more
- Handles call transfers, lead qualification, and more
- Supports English, Spanish, and French


#### Cons


- Free tier is limited to about 10 calls per month


[Sona](https://www.quo.com/sona) is an AI phone answering service built into Quo, which is a business phone system for startups and fast-growing teams. It captures key details from callers, transfers calls, and provides instant call summaries so you can follow up faster.


You can also create custom jobs in Sona. These jobs are instructions that can be used for handling specific call situations like[lead qualification](https://www.quo.com/blog/lead-qualification/) , taking a message, and providing information.


Here’s how it works:


- Sona answers the phone before the call goes to voicemail
- It gives a custom greeting based on where the caller is in your[call flow](https://www.quo.com/blog/call-flow/)
- It listens to the caller’s request
- Then it either answers the question, transfers the call, or takes a message for a callback
- You can also set a custom job so that during a phone call Sona can send a text message; for example if they want to schedule an appointment, Sona texts them a booking link
- After the call, it generates a transcript and summary of what the caller shared


Sona also handles the contacts that never become a phone call with[SMS lead capture](https://www.quo.com/sona#leads-over-sms) . If someone texts your business number, or hangs up before you pick up, it follows up by text, answers their question, and collects their details. Most services on this list are voice-only.


You can easily train Sona with key business info — like your pricing, hours, and FAQs. It also improves continuously based on customer feedback, and you’ll benefit from new features as they roll out.


Sona works seamlessly with the rest of your Quo communication, giving you full visibility into every conversation without switching platforms.


You can use Quo and Sona together to:


- Split responsibility for calls and texts with[shared numbers](https://www.quo.com/blog/how-to-share-a-business-phone-number-with-your-team/)
- Get context and action items from past conversations with[call transcripts](https://www.quo.com/features/call-transcriptions) and summaries
- Automate text messages with auto-replies and scheduled messages
- [Use AI to analyze phone calls](https://www.quo.com/blog/ai-to-analyze-phone-calls/) and spot[call drivers](https://www.quo.com/blog/call-drivers/) by organizing call recordings by topic, sentiment, or keywords


The best part? You can Quo and Sona in-app with a[free seven-day trial](https://my.quo.com/signup) before confirming they’re a fit for your business or call flow. Then if you have an existing number, easily move a US, Canadian, or North American toll-free number to Quo.


Here’s what one customer said:


*“Quo’s prices are very reasonable, and the API is pretty easy to implement. I also like how well the organization systems are set up. On top of that, I really love the AI tools that let me affordably use an AI receptionist when I can’t take calls.”*


—[Verified G2 reviewer](https://www.g2.com/products/quo-quo/reviews/quo-review-13417368)


Want to learn more first?


See Sona in action below:


#### Key features of Sona


- 24/7 availability
- Easy to set up
- Shared team inbox with Sona conversation history
- Call recordings, transcripts, and summaries
- Call tags for automatically labeling calls
- Custom phone menus
- Third-party integrations with 8,000+ tools
- English, Spanish, and French language support
- Mid-call SMS to callers
- Call transfers
- Casual and formal voice and tone options
- SOC 2 Type II certified


#### Sona pricing


[Voice AI pricing](https://www.quo.com/blog/voice-ai-pricing/) for Sona is available as an add-on to any Quo plan with these credit tiers:


Tier 1 Tier 2 Tier 3 Tier 4 Tier 5


Sona tiers Free $25 per month $49 per month $99 per month $199 per month


Included credits 1,000 credits/10 calls 4,000 credits/40 calls 10,000 credits/100 calls 25,000 credits/250 calls 60,000 credits/600 calls


Overage rate per call $1.00 $0.75 $0.65 $0.55 $0.45


Quo itself has three plans to choose from:


- **Starter:** $15 per user per month for shared phone numbers, voicemail transcriptions, unlimited calls and texts in the US and Canada, and dozens of ways to streamline your business’s phone communication
- **Business:** $23 per user per month for phone menus, call transcripts, call transferring, and more advanced features
- **Scale:** $35 per user per month for call tags, dedicated onboarding, and priority chat and email support


### 2. Rosie AI: Best for email and text notifications


#### Pros


- Detailed call documentation
- Bilingual support
- Spam filtering


#### Cons


- Requires call forwarding
- Customer conversation history stored on its platform


[Rosie](https://www.quo.com/blog/rosie-ai-alternatives/) is an answering service for small businesses that sends real-time email and text notifications for missed calls. All plans come with call transcripts, summaries, and recordings. With Zapier integrations, you can automatically send call records to your CRM. Rosie also offers English and Spanish support to provide better customer experiences across multilingual customer bases.


There’s a free seven-day trial, which is great for business owners who want to try before they buy. Once that ends, you’ll need to upgrade to a paid tier, starting at $49 per month for up to 250 minutes.


Just keep in mind the starter plan doesn’t include appointment links or call transfers, which are only available on the $149 per month tier. And if you manage multiple locations or want custom CRM integrations, you’ll need to contact sales for the Enterprise plan, which has no public pricing.


Another important caveat: Rosie is a standalone phone answering system, so you’ll have to forward calls to it from your existing phone service. This means you’ll need to toggle between apps to piece together conversation histories.


#### Key features of Rosie AI


**


- Free seven-day trial
- Appointment links with upgrade
- Spam detection
- Zapier integrations
- Live transfers with upgrade


#### Rosie AI pricing


**


Rosie has three plans to choose from:


- **Professional:** $49 per month for up to 250 minutes, message taking with custom questions, smart spam detection, and English and Spanish language options
- **Scale:** $149 per month to unlock up to 1,000 minutes, appointment links, sending texts during calls, and call transfers
- **Growth:** $299 per month to unlock up to 2,000 minutes, training files and custom agent training


### 3. Goodcall: Best for third-party integrations


#### Pros


- Customer-based pricing model
- Integrations with 1,000+ tools via Zapier
- Customizable workflows


#### Cons


- Requires a new Goodcall number
- Limited data retention


Goodcall is an AI phone answering service that responds to callers with the knowledge you’ve given it. It lets you set up different skills to tell your agent how to do certain tasks. Then, you can set up flow patterns to get information from the caller.


You can also use Goodcall to connect with more than 1,000 different tools via Zapier, which is perfect for teams with large tech stacks. There are lots of creative use cases to try. For example, you can connect Goodcall to your CRM data to personalize greetings for different callers.


But you should know that Goodcall doesn’t fully integrate with existing business numbers. You can either get a new Goodcall number with your preferred area code or[conditionally forward calls](https://www.quo.com/blog/conditional-call-forwarding/) from your existing number. Either way, conversations end up split between two platforms, which makes it harder to manage follow-ups or maintain a complete call history.


Goodcall also doesn’t do well in keeping a clear communication trail since customer and call details get deleted after seven days on the base plan. There’s also a steep learning curve. If you don’t have much time to spare on setup, it might be worth considering a Goodcall alternative.


#### Key features of Goodcall


**


- Integrates with 1,000+ tools
- Performance dashboard
- Unlimited minutes and tokens on the base plan
- Call and customer information storage
- Permission-based viewing settings


#### Goodcall pricing


**


Goodcall has three pricing plans to pick from:


- **Starter:** $79 per agent per month for unlimited minutes and tokens, three team members, seven days of call and customer details, and 100 unique customers monthly
- **Growth:** $129 per agent per month for nine team members, 30 days of call and customer details, and 250 unique customers monthly
- **Scale:** $249 per agent per month for 50 team members, unlimited call and customer details, and 500 unique customers monthly


### 4. Abby Connect: Best for backup human agents


#### Pros


- Handles lead pre-qualification, intake, and routing
- Provides customer sentiment scores
- High service quality


#### Cons


- Expensive for small businesses
- Limited integrations
- Requires call forwarding


Abby Connect offers both AI and human receptionists that can capture, pre-qualify, and intake callers, route and answer calls, and schedule appointments. The mobile app also gives you access to AI-generated call summaries, transcripts, recordings, and[customer sentiment](https://www.quo.com/blog/customer-sentiment/) scores.


Abby Connect’s biggest claim to fame is its human receptionist backup. If the AI can’t answer a customer’s question, a team of five to seven live receptionists can take over.


The high[answering service cost](https://www.quo.com/blog/answering-service-cost/) for Abby Connect may be prohibitive for small businesses, with plans starting at $165 per month. You’ll also have a limited number of monthly minutes — there’s no unlimited option available on any plan.


Beyond price, feature limitations could slow you down. There’s no built-in phone number, so you’ll have to forward calls to Abby Connect. So if a team member needs to follow up with a customer later, they’ll have to piece together conversation history across multiple tools.


#### Key features of Abby Connect


**


- English and Spanish answering
- Offers live chat on separate plan
- Custom call flows
- Workflow integrations
- Human backups on demand with upgrade


#### Abby Connect pricing


**


Here’s what you’ll pay for its AI receptionist plans. Keep in mind if you choose AI answering, you get double the minutes:


- **Starter:** $165 per month for 50 live minutes or 100 AI minutes, 24/7 call handling, call flows, call transfers, FAQ answering support, workflow integrations, and backup human receptionist services
- **Essential:** $329 per month for 100 live minutes or 200 AI minutes and all features in Starter
- **Professional:** $599 per month for 200 live minutes or 400 AI minutes and all features in Starter
- **Growth:** $1,380 per month for 500 live minutes or 1,000 AI minutes and all features in Starter


### 5. Smith.ai: Best for lead intake and qualification


#### Pros


- Hybrid AI-human model with 24/7 live agent backup
- Handles lead qualification and new client intake
- Dedicated local or toll-free business number included


#### Cons


- Expensive per-call pricing model
- Not HIPAA compliant
- Inconsistent service quality in agent responses


[Smith.ai](https://www.quo.com/blog/smith-ai-alternatives/) offers AI receptionists that handle initial call screening and basic customer interactions. For example, AI agents can ask up to 10 short answer questions for intake. Agents can also escalate complex calls to live human receptionists when necessary for an extra $3 per call.


Monthly plans that cost under $500 per month don’t include custom AI prompting, custom integrations, or full-service setup and optimization. You do get a dedicated account manager on every plan besides the free one.


#### Key features of Smith.ai


**


- Direct CRM and Zapier integrations
- New client intake
- Lead qualification
- Appointment booking
- Call transfers
- Call recording, summaries, and transcripts


#### Smith.ai pricing


**


Here’s a look at[Smith.ai pricing](https://www.quo.com/blog/smith-ai-pricing/) .


**AI-handled calls:**


- **Free:** $0 per month for 25 calls
- **Pro:** $150 per month for 75 calls, $270 per month for 150 calls, or $500 per month for 300 calls
- **Enterprise:** $500 per month for 300 calls, $800 per month for 500 calls, or custom price for 1,000+ calls


**Human-handled calls:**


- $300 per month for 30 calls
- $810 per month for 90 calls
- $2,100 per month for 300 calls


Check the per-call fees for human-handled calls. For example, appointment booking costs an extra $1.50 per call, Spanish-answered calls cost $1.00 extra per call, and payment collection costs an extra $1.00 per call.


### 6. AnswerConnect: Best for live answering


#### Pros


- Professional voices create good first impressions
- Integrates with popular CRMs and business tools


#### Cons


- Setup can take longer than most answering services
- Quality varies between different agents handling your calls
- Must add contact information to see pricing


AnswerConnect uses live receptionists to answer your calls around the clock. During setup, you’ll create custom scripts that tell them how to greet callers and answer common questions.


Once live, you forward calls to their team. They can share business information, schedule appointments, take messages, or transfer urgent calls to you.


Although you have the advantage of having real people interacting with your customers, training ‌virtual assistants requires significant time and doesn’t always guarantee proper execution.


For example,[one AnswerConnect user](https://www.trustpilot.com/reviews/5d3b9658f01869069cc3db67) made test calls to check if agents followed their script. Here’s the review they left:


*“When the Agents answer the call, they are not ‘engaging’ with the caller. The Agents sound very mechanized. So it’s a give away this is an answering service.* *Also, the Agents are not following the script.”*


AnswerConnect sends instant notifications about every interaction through their mobile app, SMS, or email. However, this means you’ll need to piece together information from multiple channels, which can be time-consuming.


#### Key features of AnswerConnect


**


- Appointment scheduling and lead capture
- Bilingual support
- CRM integrations with Salesforce, Zendesk, Slack, Zapier, and more
- Instant notifications via mobile app, SMS, or email
- Offers live website chat support
- No long-term contracts
- US-based virtual receptionists


#### AnswerConnect pricing


**


Once you enter your contact information, you can see AnswerConnect’s pricing and plans. All plans except the 300-minute plan require a $49.99 setup fee.


- **200 minutes for $350 per month:** Includes basic scripting, CRM integrations, and desktop & mobile app. Additional minutes are $2.50 per minute.
- **300 minutes for $395 per month:** Includes customizable scripting and live chat. Additional minutes are $1.85 per minute.
- **400 minutes for $575 per month.** Includes customizable scripting and live chat. Additional minutes are $1.85 per minute.


### 7. Ruby Receptionist: Best for high-touch live answering


#### Pros


- US-based receptionists trained in conflict resolution and active listening
- Handles payment processing and appointment scheduling


#### Cons


- Higher pricing than most answering services
- Bilingual support is only available during business hours
- Manual call forwarding is required for non-Ruby numbers


Ruby gives you US-based receptionists who handle your business’s phone calls and live chat. You can train them to sound like real employees. They can process payments, book appointments, transfer calls, and capture leads.


Control when calls go to Ruby or straight to you, and update instructions through their app at any time. You can also keep your personal number private using Ruby’s business number as your caller ID. But since it’s a standalone service compared to[Ruby Receptionist alternatives](https://www.quo.com/blog/ruby-receptionist-alternatives/) , you’re trusting them to get call details right and relay accurate information back to you.


You’ll need to set up call forwarding manually if Ruby doesn’t host your number. Their billing can also be confusing, and some users complain about inaccurate reports.


#### Key features of Ruby


**


- HIPAA-compliant
- Bilingual support
- Outbound calling capability
- Offers live chat support
- Mobile app for call management
- Integrates with Grasshopper, Nextiva, Zapier, Clio, and other tools


#### Ruby pricing


**


Ruby offers different pricing tiers that include the same features and only differ by minute allowances:


- **50 minutes per month:** $250 per month
- **100 minutes per month:** $395 per month
- **200 minutes per month:** $720 per month
- **500 minutes per month:** $1,725 per month


##


Is an answering service the right route at all?


If you’re unsure about an answering service, you have a few other options:


- **Traditional voicemail.** While it’s better than nothing, not all callers will leave a voicemail or wait for you to return their call. They’re more likely to call a competitor.
- **Missed-call text message.** With phone services like Quo, you can automate a text message to send after a missed call, voicemail, or when someone sends a text after-hours. It’ll at least buy you some time before you can call back.
- **Auto-attendant.** An auto-attendant can direct calls automatically to someone on-call or play prerecorded information, like your business hours.
- **In-house hire.** A traditional receptionist costs around[$17.82 an hour or $37,000 a year](https://www.ziprecruiter.com/Salaries/Virtual-Receptionist-Salary) , making it more expensive than answering services (ZipRecruiter, 2026). You may get more consistency and better answering quality than with a third-party service.


##


Verdict


There’s no single solution for managing missed calls. The choice comes down to what share of your calls need a person and whether you want a second system to manage.


If most of your calls are routine and you already pay for a business phone, an AI agent built into that system is the cheapest way to stop losing calls. Platforms like Quo include one on every plan.


If a meaningful share of your calls need judgment, a hybrid service gives you a guaranteed escalation path. If almost all of your calls need live answering, it may be better to hire a live virtual receptionist during business hours and set up an AI answering service for after-hours.

##


FAQs


****What is an AI phone answering service?****


An[AI phone answering service](https://www.quo.com/answering-service) , sometimes called an AI agent or virtual receptionist, answers customer calls when your team members can’t. Instead of sending callers to voicemail, it gives customers clear expectations for when they can expect a reply. It can also guide customers with helpful next steps, like:
– Answering FAQs
– Capturing key customer details
– Automating appointment booking


AI phone answering isn’t new, but today’s tools are smarter, simpler, and sound more natural than older iterations. They can also run in the background so your team will[never miss a call](https://www.quo.com/product/call-management/never-miss-a-call) .


**How much does an answering service cost for small businesses?**


The average[cost of a virtual receptionist](https://www.quo.com/blog/virtual-receptionist-cost/) service is around $250 per month for a fixed number of call minutes. AI answering services cost a fraction of the price of legacy services, starting as low as $25 per month.


**Is there a free AI phone answering service?**


Many AI virtual receptionists offer free plans with a limited number of calls or minutes. For example, you can try Sona AI for free for up to 1,000 credits or 10 calls per month. Smith.ai lets you try your first 25 calls per month free.


**What is the best call answering service for a small company?**


The best AI receptionist is the one that meets your business needs. You should look for a provider that’s easily customizable, offers after-hours support, and can be instantly set up on your phone system, like Quo’s Sona.


**How does an AI phone answering service work?**


AI phone answering services pick up calls before they go to voicemail and let callers know they’ve reached your business. They then answer questions or capture key details so your team can respond when they’re back in the office.


**How do you set up an AI answering service?**


Each provider is different, but the general process is the same:


1. Fill in your business information and share your knowledge base.
2. Set up call handling rules, including instructions for urgent calls.
3. Connect it to a business phone number or set up call forwarding to the service.
4. Connect it to your CRM, calendar, and any other tools
5. Test, adjust, and roll out to customers.


Read the full guide to[how to set up an AI receptionist](https://www.quo.com/blog/how-to-build-an-ai-receptionist/) .


**What are the benefits of an AI virtual receptionist?**


Virtual receptionists can answer customer calls when your team can’t pick up the phone and help direct your callers to the right team member or department.
Just keep in mind that live virtual receptionists cost more than an AI phone answering service. With AI, callers can find the right team member or department, leave a message, or get answers directly from the AI software without talking to a team member.


Learn more about[what a virtual receptionist is](https://www.quo.com/blog/what-is-a-virtual-receptionist/) and how it can benefit your business.


**Which industries commonly use AI phone answering services?**


Service businesses like plumbers, electricians, and contractors most commonly use[after hours answering services](https://www.quo.com/product/ai/after-hours-answering-service) . Real estate agents, legal practices, and healthcare providers use them as well.
These industries benefit from automated call handling, since missed calls often mean lost business opportunities and revenue.


**Can AI answering replace human receptionists?**


AI answering services are great at handling routine calls, basic scheduling, and frequently asked questions. But they can’t fully replace human receptionists for complex situations requiring empathy or nuanced problem-solving.
The best approach for most businesses is a hybrid model where AI handles simple tasks and transfers complex calls to human reps when needed.


**What’s the best AI answering service for my industry?**


The best AI answering service depends on what your callers typically need. If you’re a medical practice handling patient intake, look for HIPAA-compliant options like Lucy AI by Curious Thing or Synthflow AI’s Enterprise plan.


If your team fields a mix of sales leads and support calls, a service with lead qualification, escalation, and appointment booking — like Sona or Smith.ai — will give you the most flexibility. And if you just need basic message-taking and answering common questions, a straightforward option like Rosie or Dialzara can handle that without added complexity.
